satellyte.outcome: Turns public buying signals into enriched, scored leads for B2B revenue teams.

cover.alt: Abstract signal map representing Satellyte lead intelligence workflows

screenshots: Signal radars, each with its own ICP, lead count, and run status.
Lead table with score, signal type, source radar, enriched email and phone, and status.
AI discovery turning a plain-language prompt into matching companies.
Company drawer listing decision-makers grouped by seniority.
Integration settings for Slack, HeyReach, Instantly, and a custom webhook API.

overview: Satellyte is an AI-powered B2B sales intelligence platform. It watches public buying signals, turns them into scored leads with contact data already attached, and pushes those leads into the tools a revenue team already uses.
features: Signal radars that run 10+ buying-signal strategies continuously in the background.
A lead workspace showing score, signal type, source radar, location, and status for every lead.
Multi-provider contact enrichment with fallbacks, so one provider failing does not empty the result.
AI discovery: describe the company or person you want in plain language and get matching results.
Company view that lists decision-makers by seniority and can go find more of them.
Integrations with Slack, HeyReach, and Instantly, plus a custom webhook API.
LinkedIn engagement automation and AI-assisted content workflows.
Credit-metered public REST API, Stripe billing with idempotent webhooks, and Docker/GHCR delivery.
responsibilities: Built the Next.js product interface, from the radar and lead workspaces to the settings surface.
Built the Fastify services, the BullMQ signal engine, and the background jobs behind every long-running task.
Orchestrated the enrichment providers behind one normalized workflow with fallbacks.
Built the browser automation layer, including per-account safety limits.
Built the public API, its credit metering, authentication, and rate limiting.
Owned production delivery through Docker, GHCR, and GitHub Actions.

palmgrade.outcome: Grades palm fruit from three live industrial camera feeds and surfaces results to operators in real time.

cover.alt: Abstract camera frames and detection boxes representing Palmgrade computer vision

overview: Palmgrade grades palm fruit as it passes three production camera feeds, and puts the result in front of factory operators while the batch is still on the line.
features: Live inference on three camera feeds at once, using YOLO, OpenCV, and TensorRT behind a FastAPI service.
Operator dashboard covering all three production lines, updated live over Server-Sent Events.
AI capture viewer for reviewing exactly what the model saw on a graded batch.
Role-based access separating operators from supervisors.
Offline-tolerant event delivery: local buffering and batch sync with UUID idempotency keys, so a retry never duplicates a reading.
responsibilities: Built the Python inference service around the vision models and the camera pipeline.
Built the TypeScript API, the event path, and the role-based access rules.
Built the Next.js operator dashboard and the AI capture viewer.
Designed the buffering and synchronization strategy for unstable factory connectivity.
Packaged the stack as versioned containers for deployment inside the plant.

ai-recruitment-platform.outcome: Combines applicant screening, voice interviews, recruiter workflows, and usage-based billing in one product.

cover.alt: Abstract candidate pipeline representing the AI recruitment platform

overview: A multi-tenant recruitment product that carries hiring from job setup and candidate intake through screening, interviews, and subscription billing, without splitting the process across separate tools.
features: Job management with drag-and-drop candidate pipelines.
AI CV screening that returns structured, reviewable scores instead of one opaque verdict.
Voice-based AI interviews, with results attached to the candidate record.
Interview scheduling and a recruiter dashboard for the whole pipeline.
Stripe checkout, plans, usage metering, and webhooks that cannot be applied twice.
Tenant and role boundaries enforced through JWT, with Redis caching on high-read paths.
responsibilities: Built the layered TypeScript backend and the tenant data boundaries.
Built the JWT role model, the caching layer, and the public API surface.
Built the AI screening and voice interview workflows, and the structured results they persist.
Integrated Stripe billing end to end, including idempotent webhook processing.
Built the recruiter-facing dashboard.

internal-erp-platform.outcome: Connects Sales, Purchasing, Inventory, and Production around one consistent operational flow.

cover.alt: Sanitized ERP dashboard showing operational modules

overview: An internal ERP platform that connects the daily Sales, Purchasing, Inventory, and Production processes so one operational document flow runs across all four departments.
features: Sales and purchasing documents that follow one consistent business flow.
Inventory and production modules tied to those documents.
Role-based access, so each department only reaches what it should.
Search, filtering, and pagination across every module.
Spreadsheet exports and cross-document navigation for traceability.
responsibilities: Built the frontend modules and the shared interaction patterns reused across them.
Developed the REST API behavior behind each operational document.
Modeled the data across PostgreSQL and MongoDB, per record shape.
Translated the staff's real workflows into product features.
Kept workflow rules in backend services rather than scattered across the UI.

factory-monitoring-system.outcome: Moves plant sensor readings from MQTT ingestion to dashboards and scheduled mobile reports.

cover.alt: Abstract sensor traces representing the factory monitoring system

overview: A factory monitoring stack that collects, stores, visualizes, and reports plant sensor data, so supervisors get operational visibility from their phone instead of the control room.
features: Containerized pipeline from MQTT through Node-RED into TimescaleDB.
Grafana dashboards for live plant conditions.
Scheduled chart summaries delivered through Telegram.
Excel exports for reporting outside the dashboard.
Each service restarts independently, so one failure does not take the stack down.
responsibilities: Connected the MQTT sources to Node-RED processing.
Set up time-series storage for continuous sensor readings.
Configured the Grafana views supervisors actually use.
Built the TypeScript Telegram reporting service and its schedules.
Packaged the whole stack with Docker Compose.
